objective: Harden ordinary teaching operation backup restore routes so unsafe backup identifiers are rejected before external restore-drill planning can echo them.

codeReferences.summary: The backup restore route now resolves and validates backupId before external restore-drill planning or local backup lookup.
The route-level backup safe-id guard returns a stable redacted 400 error for unsafe backup ids.
Regression proves unsafe backup restore ids do not produce restorePlan output or local writes.

redGreenEvidence.observedFailure: The route returned 409 with an external restorePlan that echoed the unsafe path-like backup id in restorePlan.backupId and the restore-drill route.

securityPosture.ordinaryTeachingRoute: Backup restore now rejects unsafe backup ids before external restorePlan generation, local backup lookup, ownership lookup, restore writes, or audit writes.
securityPosture.rbacBoundary: Teacher authentication and production auth-provider readiness still run first; unsafe backup ids are denied immediately after that trusted identity boundary and before restore resource planning.
securityPosture.redaction: The unsafe path-like backup id, secret-like fragment, restore-drill route, and local data directory are not echoed in the fixed response.
securityPosture.productionPersistence: The regression uses production-style external teaching-operation storage selection and proves no restorePlan is produced for unsafe backup ids.

aggregateEnterpriseGateImpact.summary: This closes a narrow ordinary teaching direct-call redaction and restore-planning gap. The full enterprise gate still requires same-run owner-approved production evidence for env placement, deployment, storage, ordinary teaching route/browser smokes, app-auth readiness, browser workflow smoke, and live provider generation.
